ScaRe-tistics Data - Disney

Disneyland opened in Anaheim, California, on July 17, 1955.

For over ten years, there were no recorded deaths in the park.

That didn’t last long.

Deaths at

On June 17, 1966, a man was stuck and dragged by the monorail. The next year a 16-year-old boy was crushed by the PeopleMover.

The 1970s saw the opening of Disney World in Florida in 1971. Between the two parks there were four recorded deaths: two drownings, a fire, and woman who suffered an incident on Space Mountain.

There was a huge uptick in deaths in the 1980s across both parks. Causes of death included multple drownings, guests suffering from unknown health issues, a decapitation on the Matterhorn, and multiple plane crashes.

The 1990s saw only 9 deaths. This relatively safe period included several people who fell to their deahts, at least one suicide, and one person struck by a moving car.

The early 2000s ended that relatively safe period. Perhaps driven by increased reporting, there was another spike in deahts. The majority of these deaths, however, were due to the guest’s own health issues.

In the 2010s there were 25 deaths. The most deadly year was 2010, with 5 deaths, matching the record highs of 1982 and 1984. Several of the deaths were by suicide.

One of the most tragic deaths was in 2016, when2-year-old Lane Graves was killed by an alligator at the Grand Floridian Hotel.

The data includes deaths into 2023, with health issues among guests again dominating.
